subject: a small HTTP API that turns long URLs into short codes and redirects visitors
conclusion: Every request takes the same path: authenticate, check the rate limit, route, validate, store and send the response.
why: One handler chain means every route gets the same checks. A route never has to remember to authenticate or to limit callers.

glossary.definition: a counter that refills at a fixed rate; each request spends one token
the seven-letter key that stands for one stored URL

flow.title: One request through the API
flow.text: A staged process: every request passes the same checks in order before a route handles it.

items.label: Request
items.desc: The handler reads the method, the path, the token and the body of each request.

items.label: Auth
items.desc: The auth check turns a bearer token into an owner, or leaves the caller anonymous.

items.label: Rate limit
items.desc: A token bucket per client refuses the request with status 429 when the client is too fast.

items.label: Route
items.desc: The router matches the method and the path against one table of routes.

items.label: Validate
items.desc: The validator accepts only an http or https URL with a host and a sane length.

items.label: Store
items.desc: The store writes the link to SQLite under a new random short code.

facts.text: A redirect answers with status 302 and a Location header.
A short code has seven characters from an alphabet without look-alike letters.

inferred: Two server processes on one database would share links but not rate-limit state, because the buckets live in memory.

lines.name: arrive
lines.text: Every request starts in one handler.

lines.name: checks
lines.text: First the API checks the token, then the rate limit.

lines.name: route-and-store
lines.text: Then the router picks a route, which validates the input and stores the link.

lines.name: success
lines.text: A valid request gets status 201 and the new short code.

lines.name: refusals
lines.text: A missing token gets 401, and a caller that is too fast gets 429.
